institutionName: UiT The Arctic University of Norway

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
A scandinavian or english speaking country, to ensure that i would be able to communicate with hospital staff and patients.
A destination with different culture or nature to explore in my free time.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: As a medical student it would have been nice to not be the only one. Copenhagen used to have two spots but apparently now they only have one. Would be very nice to have someone to do all the application/registration stuff with and also to know one person when arriving there.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I had to email the hospital departments to get in touch and know when and where to show up. The erasmus coordinator gave me the email adresses and names of who to contact. So it was okay but not easy.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The erasmus coordinator at my faculty was assisting me (emailing back and forth)

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: No orientation for me since my exchange dit not start at the beginning of the semester. I found out quite late that there was an orientation week some weeks before my arrival. Unfortunately the semester in Tromsø starts in january where as my semester usually starts in february so students coming from Copenhagen will probably always have exams at home at the time of orientation week.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Easy since there is an official website for applying for student housing in Tromsø (samskipnaden). However no information regarding how long the waiting list is, so i was quite worried.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
Apply as soon as possible, you can upload documentation of acceptance to the university later on. But just apply so you are on the waiting list.
The dorms are not social at all. The kitchen is not guaranteed to be equipped so you may need to spend some money on kitchen stuff.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Complicated. Many documents to upload, and unfortunately the workflow and order of these documents were not in agreement with the guidance i got from my home university. I almost gave up during this process.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The official university website was not much help, and when i emailed the contact person from UiT exchange, they were not any help either and only referred me back to the website. A lot of trial and error and much frustration.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I registered for a traineeship, no courses. This registration was successful and i was asked which hospital departments i wished to go to and was granted my first priority.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Expect to spend a lot of time and emailing back and forth. Try to fill out the documents as best as possible and they will probably contact you if something is missing/not filled out correctly.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: 12 week clinical rotation as a medical student

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Quite similar (clinical rotation)

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: 12 week clinical rotation (anesthesiology, orthopedics and pulmonary medicine)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: 12 week clinical rotation

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: kitchen supplies. also had to buy a trash can, clothing hangers, and towels since i could not pack these.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Cheese and beer is expensive. Public transportation is fair priced (you can buy monthly passes for the busses)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Many different. I participated in knitting group and considered joining cross-country group but ended up meeting people outside of the clubs so did not have to. But there are so many groups so i am sure there is someting for everyone!

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Knitting group, social runs with Arctic Blizzard Running (not a university group, but open for everyone).

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Cross country skiing, alpine skiing, hiking, rent a car and go on day trips to Kvaløya, Sommarøya, Senja, Lyngen (you can borrow equiptment at Turbo if you buy a sim card for 50 NOK to get a norwegian phone number). DNT has cabins you can book a bed in (one person in your group needs to be a member of DNT to have a key). Sauna at Pust in the city centre.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I did not meet any norwegian medical students during my exchange. but the hospital staff was very nice and easy to socialize with.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Exploring the outdoors

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. the registration and application process is horrible but if i can do it, so can you
2. it is very nice to have a car or rent one to go on trips (try get around for private renting)
3. a very beautiful destination with easy access to outdoor activities!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is a erasmus chat group on whatsapp and facebook groups where you can meet people. otherwise just join some of the activity clubs or go on social runs in the city

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Outdoor experiences (skiing, hiking)

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: mostly the application process prior to the exchange. and now after the exchange there are many documents as well..

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
